insights.title: Locomotion is now a commodity
insights.body: The floor price of a walking humanoid fell from Unitree's G1 at about US$16,000 in 2024 to roughly US$13,500, then to the Unitree R1 (~US$5,900) and Noetix N2 (~US$5,500) in 2025. A sub-$10k robot can walk, run and recover from a shove. What is scarce now is reliable hands and autonomy, not legs.

insights.title: The center of gravity moved east
insights.body: Of the robots cataloged here, China (30) has edged past the United States (26) and Japan (25). But Japan's entries are heavily historical — WABOT, ASIMO, the HRP line, QRIO — while almost all of China's arrived from 2023 onward.

insights.title: Two counter-currents run through the hype
insights.body: Open source: Tiangong, Fourier N1, UC Berkeley's Humanoid Lite and K-Scale publish full hardware and software (9 fully-open entries, 21 more partly open). And 'drop the legs': Reflex, Galaxea, Astribot and much of the Chinese cohort put the humanoid torso on a wheeled base for cost and uptime.

insights.title: Hydraulics peaked at the DARPA Robotics Challenge
insights.body: Around half of DRC-era robots with a stated actuation type were hydraulic; in the current wave it is near zero. Boston Dynamics retiring the hydraulic Atlas for an all-electric one in 2024 was the closing bracket on that approach.

insights.title: Manipulation is the frontier
insights.body: This index tracks 15 dexterous hands as their own class. Hand degrees of freedom — Tesla's ~22, the Shadow Hand's 24 — are pushing total robot DOF up, and every well-funded program frames dexterous hands plus the perception to use them as the hard, unsolved part.

insights.title: The money arrived before the product
insights.body: Apptronik closed a US$935M Series A; Figure committed US$3.5B to compute; Agility is going public via a ~US$2.5B SPAC; Unitree's Shanghai IPO closed up nearly 500% on day one. Shipped units, by contrast, are still counted in the hundreds to low thousands.

insights.title: Factory pilots are the first real economic test
insights.body: The 2024 BMW, Mercedes-Benz and UBTECH-at-BYD pilots became 2026 fleet commitments: Schaeffler's 1,000 AEON units by 2032, Agility's US$300M+ Digit v5 order book. Whether the unit economics beat human labor and fixed automation is still unproven.

developments.title: OpenAI confirms it will build its own humanoid
developments.summary: Sam Altman: "We will definitely do a humanoid. We will do other form factors as well." The program covers hardware plus the physical-AI model; no prototype, timeline or manufacturing partner has been disclosed.

developments.title: Figure AI signs a US$3.5B compute deal with Nscale
developments.summary: Up to 100,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs, first deployments targeted for late 2027 in Texas, to train Figure's Helix vision-language-action model. The companies signaled intent to scale the arrangement past US$6B.

developments.title: Galaxea Dynamics unveils the NEXO wheeled humanoid
developments.summary: Shown at the World Robot Conference: a 168 cm / 85 kg dual-arm humanoid on a wheeled base, 30 DOF (12 in the hands), whole-body force sensing and about eight hours of runtime, aimed at commercial service and logistics.

developments.title: Humanoids beat human track records at the World Humanoid Robot Games
developments.summary: About 2,000 robots from 666 teams and 16 countries competed in Beijing. Tiangong robots beat the human world records for the 100 m, 400 m, 1,500 m and high jump; the games also showed, on live TV, how unreliable dynamic control still is.

developments.title: Unitree Robotics IPOs on Shanghai's STAR Market
developments.summary: The first publicly traded pure-play humanoid company. Priced near a US$9B valuation, the stock closed up nearly 500% on its first day amid heavy retail demand.

developments.title: Agility Robotics unveils Digit v5 and plans to go public
developments.summary: Digit v5 adds swappable hands, a ~23 kg lift and a 'cooperatively safe' design for working fence-free alongside people, with 20-hour shifts via rapid charging; Agility reports US$300M+ in multi-year orders and is merging with a SPAC at roughly US$2.5B.

developments.title: 1X starts full-scale NEO production; consumer pre-orders open
developments.summary: The home humanoid NEO is priced at US$20,000 (or US$499/month), with first deliveries to US homes targeted for end of 2026. Early units are partly teleoperated, with a human-in-the-loop learning from real home environments.

developments.title: Schaeffler commits to 1,000 Hexagon AEON humanoids by 2032
developments.summary: Following a 2025 pilot, Schaeffler will deploy at least 1,000 AEON humanoids across its global factory network over seven years, and will supply its high-precision actuators to Hexagon Robotics. AEON units began training in Schaeffler's 'Humanoid Gym' in August 2026.

developments.title: Tesla converts a Fremont line to Optimus V3
developments.summary: A former Model S/X line at Fremont is being retooled for Optimus V3, with low-volume production targeted for later in 2026. Musk called the ramp "impossible to predict" — 10,000 unique parts — and declined to give a 2026 unit target.

developments.title: Apptronik raises US$520M; deepens Google DeepMind partnership
developments.summary: The round, co-led by B Capital and Google, brings Apptronik's Series A to about US$935M at a US$5B valuation. Apollo's AI is being built with Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics models.

developments.title: Boston Dynamics to ship its first commercial electric Atlas units
developments.summary: Production for 2026 is fully committed to Hyundai and Google DeepMind. At CES 2026, Boston Dynamics and Google DeepMind announced a partnership to run Gemini Robotics foundation models on the electric Atlas and Spot.

developments.title: NVIDIA releases Isaac GR00T N1, an open humanoid foundation model
developments.summary: The first open, customizable vision-language-action foundation model for generalist humanoids, with simulation frameworks and a synthetic-data pipeline. A successor, GR00T N2, was previewed at GTC in March 2026.
